_comment: CLAUDE.md §41 stage 4 (docs/plans/2026-09-18-close-feature-gaps.md §0.10) -- THE declared table `scripts/improve-loop.py` reads: for a repeated-failure CLUSTER's key field/value, what candidate override (if any) gets backtested against it. Read-only at runtime -- improve-loop.py never invents a candidate that is not declared here (§41: 'AI must NEVER silently rewrite the production Trading System'; a candidate this table does not name is reported as having none, never guessed).
_scope: Each override is a partial `scripts/backtest-methods.py` OPTS/CLI change: `sessions` maps to the --sessions admission-time gate (REPLACES the baseline session set for that candidate run, since the candidate is a deliberately different configuration, not a further tighten -- unlike docs/architecture/trader-constraints.json, which is tighten-only); every other key must be a literal OPTS key (scripts/backtest-methods.py OPTS dict) or improve-loop.py refuses to run the candidate.

asia.why: if a repeated LOSS cluster keys on the asia session, the declared candidate excludes it -- the thinnest-liquidity window for the crypto/CFD instruments this platform trades -- and keeps the other three.

ny_pm.why: ny_pm is the post-settlement, thinning half of the US day for XAUUSD/XAGUSD; a repeated loss cluster keyed on it is a candidate for keeping only the two windows that carry the CFD session's real participation (docs/architecture/sessions.json).

london.why: if the cluster keys on london rather than asia the thin-liquidity explanation does not apply, so this is not a pure session cut but a session cut plus a higher planned-R floor: each loss costs 1.2-1.9R net of fee (backtest-methods.py fee_R = 2*fee_pct/dist), so the ~8-loss budget a 10% cap allows must buy bigger winners.

3.why: WYCKOFF-BOOK/COMBINED-BOOK volume type 3 (high-volume reclaim, VOL.high_min_ratio) is the loosest of the three spring types (knowledge/wyckoff/modern-tools.md §2.6); a repeated loss cluster keyed on it is a declared candidate for dropping it and keeping the two tighter types.

2.why: type 2 is the mid-volume Spring (Bang 2.1, WMT p049); when it clusters as a repeated loss this candidate keeps only the tightest type AND always waits for the retest (WA p80: the Test is the confirmation), the one existing knob that buys confirmation without new engine code.

fvg.why: a 'via fvg' loss cluster means the limit DID fill and the trade still lost, so entry quality is not the fault -- payoff is. Pin the causal limit rule and raise the planned-R floor: with average_loss_R at -1.27 a 2R floor does not pay for the ~8 losses a 10% total-drawdown cap permits.

WYCKOFF-BOOK.why: 1H WYCKOFF-BOOK B->C (HTF on) is exp -0.12R/dd 19.69% -> +0.62R/dd 7.17%, a PASS. Phase-D BU/LPS entries are the late, low-cause leg of the book engine (advance.md 2.7.4) and are dropped so the cause/effect target has room to pay for the trade.

_removed_2026_09_19: Removed: via=mss, method=ICT. Both overrode `ict_disp`, which stopped being an OPTS key on 2026-09-19 (docs/audits/2026-09-19-knowledge-fidelity.md finding 11): displacement is what separates an MSS (knowledge/ict/core-a.md §3.3 R10) from a liquidity grab (R11), so the deck offers no setting for it and the engine now requires it unconditionally. The hypothesis 'try requiring displacement' is therefore already the production behaviour -- there is nothing left for the candidate to change. They are DELETED rather than rewritten because inventing a replacement hypothesis is a §41 stage-11 human decision, not this file's. A cluster keyed on `via=mss` or `method=ICT` is now reported as having no declared candidate, which is the honest answer until somebody declares one.
